newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr struggles to keep break alive.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr struggles to keep break alive.

text.p: The Australian dollar clung to a good chunk of its offshore gains at the midsession and importantly kept a grip on former US$0.7795 resistance.
Asian and European buying had put a welcome end to a week of range-trading and squeezed the currency as high as US$0.7823 overnight before mainly U.S. sales reined it back.

Local bears tried to salvage short positions by going on the offer this morning but traders reported a surprising depth of bids in the US$0.7780/90 band which had held the line so far. That, they felt, boded well for a re-test of US$0.7820 although the absence of Tokyo may delay until Europe opens.
By 12.15 pm (0215 GMT) the local dollar was manning the barricades at US$0.7798/7803 having retreated from a US$0.7823 overnight high, but was still up on Monday's late US$0.7770/75.
A break of trendline resistance around US$0.7830 was needed to build momentum and convince sceptics the rise was anymore than a blip in a long sideways consolidation.
The loss of US$0.7765 at any time would suggest it was just that and see US$0.7720 support re-tested.
On the crosses the dollar had benefited from good German and Japanese demand overnight to rise to 1.3503/16 marks from 1.3458/70 and 98.80/90 yen from 98.50/60.
In trade weighted terms it had firmed to 60.6 by midday from a previous 60.4 close.
There were no domestic data to provide direction today but a key U.S. wages report tonight could well have implications for Australian/U.S. interest differentials.
The employment cost index has been singled out by the Federal Reserve as a reliable indicator of labour costs and so is closely watched by the market.
The indicator had been surprisingly subdued during 1996 but analysts are looking for signs of upward pressure to show from the tightening labour market and from rising benefit costs.
Median forecasts favour a rise of 0.9 percent in Q1 which would take annual growth to 3.1 percent from 2.8 percent in Q4.
Some analysts see the risk on the upside given anecdotal evidence of rising health care premiums and expect a gain of more than 1.0 percent.
Such a rise would harden expectations the Fed would tighten policy again at its next meeting on May 20 and would likely see the A$'s yield advantage over the U.S. dollar erode further.
In that case, the local unit could well find itself testing support tonight.
